intro: Assisted stretch therapy is a one-to-one session where a clinician moves and supports your body through a series of targeted stretches while you relax. You stay fully clothed throughout — it isn’t massage, and it isn’t a yoga class.

At Exhale it’s osteopath- and physiotherapist-led. Every client starts with a movement screen, so your stretches are planned around how your body actually moves. It’s our own clinically led method, not a one-size-fits-all routine.
ticks: Fully clothed — no oils, no getting changed
Never painful — you control the intensity

sections.title: Who is assisted stretching for?
paras: Desk workers. Long hours at a desk or behind the wheel can leave your neck, shoulders, back and hips feeling tight. Regular assisted stretching may help ease muscle tension and stiffness, and may help improve posture alongside simple changes to how you sit and move.
Active people. Whether you run, lift, cycle or play sport, sessions are designed to help you move more freely, support your training and complement your recovery.
Regular maintenance. Many people simply want to feel looser and move better week to week. A short, regular session is an easy way to stay on top of tightness before it builds up.

sections.title: The Exhale stretch method
paras: Your first session always starts with a movement screen. Your clinician looks at how you move — your posture, flexibility and range of motion through the hips, spine and shoulders — and uses it to set a baseline and plan your stretches.

Stretches are then taken slowly, with your feedback throughout, using techniques such as assisted static stretching and contract–relax (PNF) stretching. Each session builds on the last, and we re-check how you move so you can see your progress.

sections.title: Clinically led, not just a stretch
paras: Sessions are led by registered osteopaths and physiotherapists, so your clinician is trained to spot when something needs more than stretching. If you have pain, an injury or a specific problem such as back pain or sciatica, we’ll assess it properly and recommend osteopathy or physiotherapy first — with stretching as part of your plan where it helps.

Sessions are led by Hafi Rahman, our founder and principal osteopath, and Emre Tosun, physiotherapist, with the wider Exhale team being trained in the method over time. Want treatment and stretching together? Ask about our combined osteopathy and stretch session.

selfpay.title: Not claimable on health insurance
selfpay.text: Assisted stretch therapy is a self-pay service and can’t be claimed through your health insurer. If you have pain or an injury, osteopathy or physiotherapy may be covered by your policy — call us and we’ll explain your options.

How is it different from massage?

Massage works on your muscles with hands-on pressure. Assisted stretching moves you through stretches and positions to work on flexibility and range of motion. You stay fully clothed and no oils are used.
How is it different from osteopathy?

Osteopathy is assessment and treatment for pain and injury, such as back pain, neck pain or sciatica. Assisted stretching is designed to help you move more freely — it isn’t a treatment for a specific condition. If you have pain or an injury, we’ll recommend osteopathy or physiotherapy, with stretching as part of your plan where it helps. You can also book a combined osteopathy and stretch session.
Why does my first session have to be 50 minutes?

Your first session includes a movement screen before any stretching. It shows us how you move, sets your baseline, checks that stretching is suitable for you and lets us plan the right stretches. Shorter 25-minute sessions are available after that.
Can I have assisted stretching while pregnant?

Please speak to us before booking. We’ll talk through your pregnancy and health history and let you know whether assisted stretching is suitable, or whether pregnancy osteopathy would be a better fit.
Can I claim it on health insurance?
No — assisted stretch therapy is self-pay only and can’t be claimed through health insurance.
Where can I have assisted stretch therapy?
At our Sutton Coldfield clinic, 1 Sutton Oak Corner, Streetly, B74 2DH — easy to reach from Four Oaks, Aldridge, Walsall and across north Birmingham.
